standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of perfect complexes and the pseudo-coherence of modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite free resolution E^bullet of M.

standard_prerequisites.name: The last-term-flat criterion bounding flatness of a cokernel in a resolution
standard_prerequisites.use: Yields the index d at which F_d becomes flat.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finitely presented flat module is finite projective
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns flatness of F_d into finite projectivity, giving the finite resolution.

core_obligations: Assume (2) and note that the complex E^bullet with E^{-i} = F_i is quasi-isomorphic to M[0], hence M is perfect (proof lines 18930-18931).
Conversely assume (1) and use the perfect-complex and pseudo-coherence statements to find a resolution E^bullet -> M with E^{-i} finite free (proof lines 18932-18935).
Use the last-term-flat statement to conclude that F_d = Coker(E^{d-1} -> E^d) is flat for some d sufficiently large (proof lines 18936-18938).
Use the Algebra statement on finitely presented flat modules to conclude that F_d is finite projective (proof lines 18938-18940).
Conclude that 0 -> F_d -> E^{-d+1} -> ... -> E^0 -> M -> 0 is the desired resolution (proof lines 18941-18945).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a module M over a ring R and proves the equivalence of two conditions: M is a perfect module, and there exists a resolution 0 -> F_d -> ... -> F_1 -> F_0 -> M -> 0 with each F_i finite projective (source lines 18916-18927). Part of the proof is immediate: assuming (2), the complex E^bullet with E^{-i} = F_i is quasi-isomorphic to M[0], hence M is perfect (proof lines 18930-18931). The substantive direction is (1) implies (2). By the perfect-complex statement and the statement on pseudo-coherence of modules, one can find a resolution E^bullet -> M with each E^{-i} finite free (proof lines 18932-18935). By the last-term-flat statement, the cokernel F_d = Coker(E^{d-1} -> E^d) is flat for d sufficiently large (proof lines 18936-18938). The Algebra statement on finitely presented flat modules then gives that F_d is finite projective (proof lines 18938-18940). The desired resolution is then the truncated one 0 -> F_d -> E^{-d+1} -> ... -> E^0 -> M -> 0 (proof lines 18941-18945). The non-routine content is the choice of d large enough that the cokernel becomes flat, which converts a possibly infinite free resolution into a finite projective one.
